title: Residue-field algebra structure and reduction of a chosen generating family
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $C$ be a commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and let $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ be a finite family generating $C$ over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with $n=0$ allowed. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and $D=C/\mathfrak m C$, where $\mathfrak m C$ is the ideal generated by the images of elements of $\mathfrak m$. Then $k$ is a field [def-weil-field] and is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The map $A\to C\to D$ induces a $k$-algebra structure on $D$, characterized by $(a\bmod\mathfrak m)\mapsto(a\bmod\mathfrak m C)$. The classes $\bar c_1,\ldots,\bar c_n$ generate $D$ as a $k$-algebra. More precisely, the image in $D$ of any polynomial expression in the $c_i$ with coefficients in $A$ is the same expression in the $\bar c_i$ with every coefficient reduced modulo $\mathfrak m$. In particular $D$ is a finite type $k$-algebra.

source.place: Tags 00F3 (definition-finite-type), reduction of a polynomial generating family, and 00FM (section-Noetherian), applied to the residue field; the residue-field fact is also recalled in fields.tex, section-examples.

proof.text: The unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is maximal, so [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field] applied to $R=A$, $I=\mathfrak m$ gives that $k=A/\mathfrak m$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 09FB (section-introduction), residue field of a local ring

proof.text: Every ideal $J$ of $k$ is either zero or contains some $x\ne0$. In the latter case $1=x^{-1}x\in J$, so $J=k$. Thus $J$ is generated by the empty set or by $1$. By [def-weil-field] and [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $k$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FM (section-Noetherian), opening definition; fields.tex Tag 09FB explains the two ideals of a field

proof.text: Write $\alpha:A\to C$ for the structure map and $q:C\to D$ for the quotient map of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Define $\beta:k\to D$ by $\beta([a])=q(\alpha(a))$. If $[a]=[b]$, then $a-b\in\mathfrak m$, hence $\alpha(a-b)\in\mathfrak m C$ and $q(\alpha(a))=q(\alpha(b))$. This proves well-definedness. Addition, multiplication and the unit are preserved because $q\alpha$ preserves them. Every class has a representative, so this formula also gives uniqueness. The ring map $\beta$ is the required $k$-algebra structure by the same definition.

source.place: Tags 00AQ (section-conventions) and 00AR (section-rings-basic): quotient rings and algebras

proof.text: For a finite polynomial expression $P=\sum_e a_e\prod_{i=1}^n X_i^{e_i}$, put $\bar c_i=q(c_i)$. Since $q$ preserves finite sums, products and powers and $q\alpha(a_e)=\beta([a_e])$, directly $q(P(c))=\sum_e\beta([a_e])\prod_i\bar c_i^{e_i}$. This is precisely the coefficient-reduction formula. Given $d\in D$, choose $c\in C$ with $q(c)=d$ using the surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and write $c=P(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The formula expresses $d$ as a polynomial over $k$ in the specified $\bar c_i$, proving generation and finite type. Empty products are $1$, so the argument includes $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 00F3 (definition-finite-type), clause (1), reduction of the specified polynomial expressions

lean.statement: theorem residue_algebra_finite_type_model (A : Type u) (C : Type v) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin n → C) (hc : Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := A) c)) : IsField (ResidueField A) ∧ IsNoetherianRing (ResidueField A) ∧ ∃ β : ResidueField A →+* C ⧸ (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C), (∀ a : A, β (residue A a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C)) (algebraMap A C a)) ∧ (∀ γ : ResidueField A →+* C ⧸ (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C), (∀ a : A, γ (residue A a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C)) (algebraMap A C a)) → γ = β) ∧ Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom β (fun i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C)) (c i))) ∧ (∀ P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A, Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C)) (MvPolynomial.aeval c P) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ β (fun i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A C)) (c i)) (MvPolynomial.map (residue A) P)) ∧ β.FiniteType
